cohort: 311 pregnant patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection (exposure group) and 205 uninfected pregnant patients (control group)
finding: Mild COVID-19 infection during pregnancy was not associated with detrimental effects on most maternal and neonatal outcomes, but was associated with increased cesarean section and fetal distress.
mod_finding: Pregnant women infected with SARS-CoV-2 had a significantly higher incidence of cesarean section compared to uninfected pregnant women.
